sentences.text: The genus Gladioserratus includes three known species: G. aptiensis, G. magnus, and G. dentatus.
It belongs to the family Hexanchidae and is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, which contains cartilaginous fish.
This animal lived between 137.05 and 61.66 million years ago, spanning from the Valanginian to the Danian stages.
The species G. dentatus was originally described from fossils found in the Valanginian of France.
Teeth discovered in the middle Danian Faxe Formation at Faxe, Denmark, extend the genus's known range into the Paleocene.

While the original authors described the genus as containing species that lived from the Hauterivian to the Cenomanian stages, researchers suggest that assigning Notorynchus serratissimus to Gladioserratus would extend the genus's range to the early Eocene.
